DECK: Discipleship Experience (Section 6) Prayer

Q1. Which statement best captures the lesson's treatment of prayer's cumulative effect?
A. Prayer produces gradual spiritual strengthening through consistent investment.
B. Prayer becomes effective mainly through longer individual sessions.
C. Prayer becomes most important when serious spiritual problems arise.
D. Prayer accumulates mainly through increasing the number of requests made.
ANSWER: A

Q2. Why does the lesson warn against making "God, help me" the entirety of one's prayer life?
A. Prayer should go beyond emergency requests while still making room for short prayers.
B. Short prayers lack effectiveness without extended declarations.
C. God requires every prayer to contain a detailed account of the situation.
D. Short prayers are appropriate mainly when engaging in spiritual warfare.
ANSWER: A

Q3. According to the teaching, "not praying" is dangerous primarily because it:
A. prevents God from knowing what the believer needs.
B. gradually weakens the believer's capacity to withstand pressure.
C. limits the believer's ability to receive immediate answers.
D. causes the believer to lose salvation through inconsistent devotion.
ANSWER: B

Q4. What principle is captured by "If you cannot fly, run; if you cannot run, walk; if you cannot walk, crawl"?
A. Believers should change their spiritual routine whenever life becomes difficult.
B. Spiritual consistency is less important than doing something occasionally.
C. The way you engage may change, but you should keep moving toward God.
D. Difficult seasons mean believers should expect less from themselves.
ANSWER: C

Q5. A believer prays for an hour, feels nothing, and concludes the prayer was ineffective. What has the lesson identified as the primary error?
A. Measuring spiritual progress by how strongly you feel.
B. Spending too much time in prayer.
C. Assuming prayer must always be emotional.
D. Thinking prayer only works when it produces an immediate result.
ANSWER: A

Q6. What does "we walk by faith and not by sight" require in the context of the lesson?
A. Trusting spiritual feelings more than what Scripture says.
B. Refusing to look at any evidence of spiritual growth.
C. Choosing faith-filled experiences over regular prayer.
D. Trusting spiritual realities even when you cannot see or feel them.
ANSWER: D

Q7. What is the lesson's function of Hebrews 11:6 in relation to prayer?
A. It teaches that prayer should always produce a noticeable response.
B. It moves the believer's confidence away from feelings and toward God.
C. It teaches that praying longer will make you feel closer to God.
D. It shows that long prayer is the main requirement for answered prayer.
ANSWER: B

Q8. Which assumption does the statement "Prayer will never be a waste of time" directly confront?
A. Prayer must always be long to be valuable.
B. Prayer is only useful when combined with fasting.
C. If nothing happens immediately, the prayer achieved nothing.
D. Prayer does not work when you do not feel strongly about it.
ANSWER: C

Q9. Why does Apostle say "pray like you're close to God"?
A. How close you see yourself to God should shape how you approach Him.
B. Feeling far from God always means you have not prayed enough.
C. People become close to God only after spending many hours in prayer.
D. God answers people differently based on how close they feel to Him.
ANSWER: A

Q10. The lesson uses Jesus' statement "Father, I thank you that you always hear me" primarily to cultivate:
A. confidence that every prayer will be answered immediately.
B. confidence that every request made in faith will be granted.
C. confidence in the believer's ability to pray correctly.
D. confidence that God hears even when the prayer experience does not feel special.
ANSWER: D

Q11. Why does Philippians 2:13 become particularly encouraging to the believer who knows they should be doing better?
A. Wanting to improve guarantees that behaviour will change immediately.
B. Wanting to improve means the believer has already overcome the problem.
C. The desire to improve is itself a sign that God is working in them.
D. God takes full responsibility for keeping the believer's prayer life strong.
ANSWER: C

Q12. Which response best represents the full posture the lesson teaches toward struggling with prayer?
A. Recognise the struggle → accept it → wait until you feel stronger → start again.
B. Recognise the struggle → work harder → remove the weakness → maintain the standard.
C. Recognise the struggle → ask for forgiveness → lower the standard → rebuild slowly.
D. Recognise the struggle → reject condemnation → receive God's help → keep going and grow.
ANSWER: D

Q13. According to the lesson, what is the primary weakness of a prayer life centered almost entirely on requests?
A. Requests are less likely to be answered when they are repeated.
B. Request-based prayer usually makes prayer sessions shorter.
C. The believer may miss prayer as a way of growing close to God.
D. God expects believers to spend more time worshipping than asking.
ANSWER: C

Q14. A believer prays the same request repeatedly because they believe "more words will eventually make God respond." Which principle from the lesson corrects this?
A. Persistence is not needed when someone has strong faith.
B. Prayer length should never be confused with a formula for making God respond.
C. God only responds when prayer is focused on intimacy.
D. Prayer length has no value at all.
ANSWER: B

Q15. According to the lesson, what is the believer's confidence concerning prayer?
A. God hears because the believer has enough spiritual authority.
B. God answers more after a believer has prayed for a long time.
C. God responds more quickly when prayer is persistent enough.
D. God hears those who ask in His name
ANSWER: D

Q16. What does Jesus' rebuke, "Couldn't you watch with me one hour?", establish within the lesson?
A. There are times when not praying enough can leave a believer unprepared for what comes next.
B. Every believer must pray for at least one hour every day.
C. Prayer is ineffective if it lasts less than an hour.
D. Long prayer is the main measure of spiritual readiness.
ANSWER: A

Q17. What distinguishes the "firefighting approach" from the culture of prayer taught in the lesson?
A. Firefighting responds when there is a crisis; prayer culture builds strength before the crisis.
B. Firefighting focuses on warfare while prayer culture focuses on thanksgiving.
C. Firefighting uses short prayers while prayer culture uses long prayers.
D. Firefighting is emotional while prayer culture is disciplined.
ANSWER: A

Q18. A Christian still prays occasionally but increasingly finds that prayer no longer shapes their spiritual experience. Which principle most directly addresses this?
A. Pray for longer until the old experience comes back.
B. Return to consistent engagement with God instead of praying only occasionally.
C. Focus mainly on spiritual warfare until the problem improves.
D. Replace personal prayer with group prayer.
ANSWER: B

Q19. Why does the lesson describe prayer as a "strategy for preserving faith"?
A. Prayer helps keep strong the believer's confidence in what God can do.
B. Prayer guarantees that believers will never doubt.
C. Prayer gives believers power to remove every difficult circumstance.
D. Prayer continually reminds believers of every doctrine they have learned.
ANSWER: A

Q20. According to the lesson's use of 1 Peter 5:8–9, what constitutes resistance to the devil?
A. Praying more spiritual warfare prayers.
B. Finding every possible strategy the enemy might use.
C. Staying firm and strong in faith.
D. Continuing to pray until all opposition stops.
ANSWER: C

Q21. What is the point of submitting to "the boredom of consistency"?
A. Repetition automatically produces spiritual power.
B. Consistency keeps spiritual strength alive even when things no longer feel new.
C. Spiritual maturity means moving from basic practices to more advanced ones.
D. Emotional prayer is unreliable, so it should be avoided.
ANSWER: B

Q22. What does the lesson identify as a major reason people struggle with long prayer?
A. They do not know enough prayer terms.
B. They do not know enough about spiritual warfare.
C. They mainly think of prayer as asking God for things.
D. They expect to have an emotional experience every time they pray.
ANSWER: C

Q23. Which shift best represents the lesson's intended correction?
A. Moving from short requests to long requests.
B. Moving from spontaneous prayer to scheduled prayer.
C. Moving from emotional prayer to highly structured prayer.
D. Moving from simply getting things from God to growing close to God.
ANSWER: D

Q24. In the teaching on Luke 11, persistence in prayer is primarily presented as:
A. A way to make God respond when He does not want to.
B. Part of developing the determination needed for a culture of prayer.
C. Proof that someone has prayed long enough for an answer.
D. A replacement for faith when an answer is delayed.
ANSWER: B

Q25. Which principle best integrates the entire teaching on prayer length, consistency, faith, and intimacy?
A. A strong prayer life is mainly measured by how long someone prays.
B. A strong prayer life is mainly shown through powerful spiritual declarations.
C. A strong prayer life mainly prepares believers to avoid future spiritual crises.
D. A mature prayer life combines consistency, spontaneous prayer, persistence, and intimacy with God.
ANSWER: D

Q26. According to the lesson, why is being able to "conveniently go three days without praying" treated as a serious warning sign?
A. It demonstrates that the believer has lost interest in spiritual things.
B. It proves that the believer has replaced God with other priorities.
C. It indicates a level of spiritual vulnerability that may not yet be externally visible.
D. It means the believer has already become spiritually ineffective.
ANSWER: C

Q27. Why does Apostle insist on not breaking the prayer streak?
A. Consistency itself guarantees spiritual protection.
B. Maintaining daily engagement helps prevent gradual spiritual deterioration.
C. Missing prayers gives the enemy immediate legal access.
D. A prayer streak is evidence that a believer has developed spiritual maturity.
ANSWER: B

Q28. The lesson's "alarm" analogy primarily challenges which assumption?
A. Spiritual danger matters only after its consequences become visible.
B. Spiritual problems usually begin with dramatic external attacks.
C. Prayer becomes valuable only when a specific problem can be identified.
D. Early discipline matters less than responding correctly after failure.
ANSWER: A

Q29. What does "pray without ceasing" mean within the framework taught?
A. Maintaining continual fellowship with God alongside scheduled prayer times.
B. Maintaining uninterrupted verbal prayer throughout the entire day.
C. Replacing scheduled prayer with spontaneous communication throughout the day.
D. Increasing prayer frequency until other daily responsibilities become secondary.
ANSWER: A
